After extensive negotiations Westmore-land Resources and the Crow Tribe agreed to amend the original leases and the Crow Tribe withdrew its petition "with prejudice" (cannot again bring the same case). The Secretary of the Interior approved the amendments to the lease as being in the best interests of the Tribe, and found that the protection of tribal interests provided by the leases differed somewhat from protection provided by regulations contained in 25CFR171. He therefore waived certain specified provisions of part 171 to the extent they were inconsistent with provisions of the amended leases. The Secretary made it clear in his order that approval of the amended leases in no way precluded him from exercising his trust responsibility in the future with regard to any aspect of the Crow Tribe's affairs.
Two amended leases resulted from the negotiations and are currently in force for the 30,876.45 acre Westmoreland Resources leasehold.

Effective date for the amended leases is November 26, 1974. The most significant changes in the Tract III lease pertain to the royalty provisions. For coal mined and shipped under previously existing contracts (totalling 76.5 million tons over 20 years) the following royalties are to be paid to the Crow Tribe:
1974-75 The greater of 25 cents per ton or 6 percent*
1976-77 The greater of 30 cents per ton or 6 percent
1977 The greater of 35 cents per ton or 6 percent
* 
Of f.o.b. mine price per ton.
